day01: hook
Day one of making my dream game!
idea1
It's a cozy little game about a pond in the woods.
idea2
The pond is full of salmon,
idea3
and bears are obsessed with salmon. They'll literally stand in a waterfall all day, just waiting for one to jump into their mouth.
idea4
So in my game, you take care of the pond, you raise the fish, and hungry bears come by to eat them.
name
I'm calling it The Bear Must Eat.
squares
For now, everything is just squares, because I want the gameplay to feel good before I draw anything.
bear
The brown square is a bear, and the orange one is the fox who owns the pond.
test
So for the first test, all the bear has to do is walk over to the pond.
through
And he walked straight through the fox,
water
and then right across the water, like it's a sidewalk.
broken
So yeah, nothing has collision yet. That's bug number one.
cta
Tomorrow I'm adding fish, so tell me what kind of fish you want to see!
day02: Day two, and today I'm adding fish!
They're still just little squares, but each one swims around on its own, so the pond already feels kind of alive.
And when two happy fish bump into each other, you get a baby fish, which is honestly my favorite thing so far.
But then I changed one tiny thing in the code, and this happened.
Every single fish swam into the same corner, and they just stayed there.
Turns out I forgot to normalize their direction, so they were all drifting the same way. That's bug number two.
Now that it's fixed, they spread out again, and the pond slowly fills itself back up.
day03: Day three! In my game, the bears all work at an office in town,
so every day at five p.m., when the office closes...
they all run straight to the pond.
They jump in, grab a fish, and pay you a few coins for it.
This is the part I've been waiting to build. I love how chaotic it is.
there were no fish left. Not a single one. They ate the whole pond.
And now they're just standing in the water, looking around like, where did the food go?
So yeah, I definitely need to balance this. That's tomorrow's problem.
day04: Day four! Today, the orange square finally gets replaced.
This square is supposed to be the fox who owns the pond, and he deserves way better than this.
So I built him cube by cube, in 3D.
He's got a top hat, a monocle, and a gold chain, because he's the richest guy in the forest.
Then I gave him way too many animations. He can dance, count his money, and even faint.
day05: Day five! Let me introduce you to the bears.
This is office bear. He walks, he eats, and he roars when he's hungry.
There's also grandma bear, construction bear, and the CEO, who tips the most.
And now, all the brown squares finally turn into real bears!
Watching them cannonball into the pond never gets old.
The rest of the world is still squares, though, so that's next.
day06: Day six. The bears look great, but the world is still made of squares.
So I spent the whole day drawing it, pixel by pixel.
Grass, trees, flowers, rocks, lily pads, and real fish swimming around.
Then I added a day and night cycle.
Night is my favorite, with the moonlight and the little fireflies.
And this is the exact same pond from day one. Crazy, right?
day07: Day seven! A lot of you have been leaving comments,
and someone asked for a banana fish. So okay, let's make a banana fish.
I drew it pixel by pixel, with little brown spots, and the stem is its tail.
Then I added it to the game as a super rare egg.
It's a banana. It's also a fish. And I'm weirdly proud of it.
And of course the bears eat it, because they eat everything.
What should I add next? Leave a comment and I might just add it!
day08: Day eight! You can finally build things now,
like a whole little restaurant right next to the pond.
Every piece lands with a little plonk and a puff of dust, which is super satisfying.
There are tables, a barbecue, a jukebox, and a big neon sign that says...
And at five p.m., the bears actually come in, sit down, and eat there.
A tiny restaurant for bears. I'm really happy with how this turned out.
day09: Day nine. The game worked, but honestly, it felt kind of dead.
Comic words, squash and stretch, screen shake, coins, and way too many sound effects.
Here's the same game, before and after.
Which one would you rather play?
day10: Day ten! I finally made a title screen.
And yes, there's always a bear in the pond. Always.
Ten days ago, this was just a brown square walking on water.
Thank you so much for following along. Should I keep going?
